data.narrative:
Arbor Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Brad Hartwig that has raised $96M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private climate-tech firms (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen) and one public peer (Linnea Oil [LNZA]), though the private set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with aligned valuation tiers to support a robust peer-median approach.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable technique here. Using the $96M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $192M. This method reflects observed venture cadence in the frontier-tech sector where companies at this stage have historically commanded 2x return multiples before follow-on rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $163M (low), $192M (median), to $221M (high), derived from sensitivity around the stage-progression step-up. The median of $192M represents the most defensible point estimate given available data. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage or tight-tier comparable transactions—a limitation common in early-stage climate tech—and reliance on a single-method triangulation. Any valuation materially outside the $163M–$221M band would require either revised assumptions about sector-standard step-up multiples or new comparable data.
